main_body: Grid of 4x3 riveted metal panel tiles (floor/wall plates) with a cyan indicator light in the right column
top_band: none. The scan shows only a dark base (L=50) with thin 1-row highlight lines (L=93 and L=70) repeating every 16 rows. These are tile edge bevels, not a standing object's top surface.
evidence: The kind is terrain: repeating autotile-style panel tiles, not a standing volume. The 3/4 top-plus-front contract does not apply to a floor or wall surface patch. Each panel has a light upper bevel, rivets and an inset recess in the centre column, and there are no isometric side faces. It is not a standing object drawn as an elevation, so I pass it as terrain.

style.evidence: Measured facts: 9 distinct colours and a median of 6 per tile, against 7 and 7 for the paving reference. That is equal to paving, though well below the grass reference (80 colours, 26 per tile). Flat-fill coverage is 0%. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outlines carry a blue-slate tint matching the metal. The panels are built from a bevel highlight, mid, dark, rivet dots and a recessed frame, and are not sticker-like. Compared with the paving reference it is at least as rich and structured, so it passes.
